key_insight: Combining tensor hypercontraction (THC) with Block-Invariant Symmetry Shift (BLISS) substantially reduces the quantum circuit cost of simulating molecular vibrations.
engineering_relevance: More efficient Hamiltonian block encodings can lower quantum phase estimation costs, while trading additional ancilla qubits for improved scaling.
method: Construct Pauli- and THC-based linear-combination-of-unitaries block encodings of second-quantized vibrational Hamiltonians.
Extend BLISS to vibrational Hamiltonians to reduce the LCU 1-norm.
Design circuits exploiting Hamiltonian factorization and Toffoli–qubit tradeoffs.
evidence_signal: For the molecules studied, BLISS-THC reduces phase-estimation Toffoli costs by more than 100× versus existing block encodings and T-gate counts by up to 9× versus recent Trotter-based methods.
watch_item: Improved scaling requires additional ancilla qubits, and the reported savings may vary with molecular system and implementation.
paper_title: Efficient Block Encodings of Vibrational Hamiltonians
